description: Figure 8 is a pie chart illustrating the distribution of problems based on their correctness under two experimental conditions: “with knowledge” (w/ knowledge) and “without knowledge” (w/o knowledge), evaluated using a zero-shot approach. The chart is divided into three distinct slices, each representing a category of problem difficulty: “Easy,” “Medium,” and “Hard.” The “Easy” category, shown in light blue, constitutes the largest portion of the chart, indicating the highest proportion of correctly answered problems. The “Medium” category, depicted in orange, represents the second-largest segment, while the “Hard” category, shown in green, makes up the smallest slice, reflecting the lowest rate of correct responses. The chart visually emphasizes that performance declines as problem difficulty increases, with the majority of correct answers concentrated in the “Easy” tier. No numerical percentages are labeled on the slices, and the legend is not visible in the provided image, but the categories are clearly distinguishable by color and relative size. The overall layout is simple and centered, with the caption positioned directly below the chart.
